fields.Front: What is Object-Oriented Design and Analysis (OODA)?
fields.Back: Designing a system using objects that represent real-world entities and interact with each other to solve a problem, structuring the system so it is modular, flexible, and easy to maintain. Analysis discovers what objects exist in the problem; design decides how they are structured and collaborate.

fields.Front: Step 1 of class design: what do you look for, and what does the online shopping example yield?
fields.Back: Look at the problem domain and identify the entities, usually real-world objects or concepts. Online shopping system: Customer, Product, Order, ShoppingCart. A practical technique is to underline the nouns in the problem description.

fields.Front: Step 2 of class design: what two questions do you ask, with the Product example?
fields.Back: What information does it need to store (attributes) and what actions must it perform (methods)? Product: attributes name, price, stockQuantity; methods getPrice(), updateStock().

fields.Front: Give the slides' example for each of association, aggregation, and inheritance.
fields.Back: Association: a Customer has an Order. Aggregation: an Order contains multiple Product objects. Inheritance: Admin and RegularUser inherit from User.

fields.Front: Which UML notation does Week 2 assign to each of the three Week 1 relationships?
fields.Back: Association: a plain solid line. Aggregation/composition: a diamond at the owner (hollow for aggregation, filled for composition). Inheritance: a solid line with a hollow triangular arrowhead pointing at the base class.

fields.Front: What is Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) as recapped in the slides?
fields.Back: Modelling real-world entities as objects; objects contain both data (attributes) and behaviour (methods) and interact with each other to perform tasks, following the principles of OOP (encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism, abstraction).

fields.Front: What seven areas of content does CS3307A cover, per the 'Concepts Covered' slide?
fields.Back: Object-oriented concepts (encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism); design patterns (apply, reuse, solve); UML diagrams (class, sequence, use case); code refactoring; quality attributes (scalability, security, performance); design specifications; software evolution.

fields.Text: The three steps for designing classes and objects: {{c1::identify objects}}, {{c1::define attributes and methods}}, {{c1::determine relationships}}.

Week 1 relationships: {{c1::Association}} = objects know about each other; {{c1::Aggregation}} = one object contains or is composed of others; {{c1::Inheritance}} = one object is a specialized version of another.
OODA designs a system using {{c1::objects}} that represent {{c1::real-world entities}} and interact to solve a problem, structuring it to be {{c1::modular, flexible, and easy to maintain}}.
Candidate objects for an online shopping system: {{c1::Customer}}, {{c1::Product}}, {{c1::Order}}, {{c1::ShoppingCart}}.
fields.Extra: A practical technique is to underline the nouns in the problem description.

fields.Text: A Product class might have attributes {{c1::name, price, stockQuantity}} and methods {{c1::getPrice(), updateStock()}}.
Relationship examples: association - a {{c1::Customer}} has an Order; aggregation - an {{c1::Order}} contains multiple Products; inheritance - {{c1::Admin and RegularUser}} inherit from User.
